FSS_13.text: To support citizens and businesses that have relocated from the capital to rural areas to engage in livestock farming and agriculture, in order to ensure a balance between urban and rural development and to curb centralisation.
FSS_13.activities: To organise the provision of preferential loans from the Local Small and Medium Enterprises Development Fund to individuals and businesses engaged in food-related activities who have relocated from the capital to local areas.

SECTORAL_6.text: Develop green economy-oriented livestock husbandry that preserves traditional nomadic cultural heritage in rangelands while establishing intensified, technology-driven farming near urban areas, sustainably using resources.
SECTORAL_6.activities:
Maintain traditional nomadic rangeland-based herding as the dominant pastoral system
Establish intensified meat and dairy farming zones near Darkhan-Uul, Selenge, and Tuv provinces
Direct cooperative investment loans toward 14 climate adaptation measures
Promote sustainable resource use through herder cooperatives

FSS_11.text: To ensure a stable supply of the infrastructure, energy, steam, heat and fuel sources required to guarantee food supply and safety and to increase domestic production of food products that replace imports.
FSS_11.sourceLabel: 2.5 Stable energy, heat, fuel for food production
FSS_11.activities:
Establish regulations to reduce or exempt the costs of steam and heat usage for major food producers and greenhouse farms.
Organise measures to ensure the stable supply of fuel and energy in order to maintain the continuity of agricultural production.
Where necessary, establish and implement arrangements to subsidise or exempt the electricity costs of staple food producers.

NBSAP_16.text: By 2030, reform subsidies and incentives that have negative impacts on biodiversity, while increasing environmentally positive (green) incentives.
NBSAP_16.activities:
16.1. Ensure intersectoral coordination in subsidy and incentive policy planning
16.2. Conduct environmental monitoring and evaluation of subsidies and incentives
16.3. Repurpose potentially harmful subsidies and incentives in the agriculture sector
16.4. Repurpose potentially harmful subsidies and incentives in the energy sector
16.5. Repurpose potentially harmful subsidies and incentives in the transport sector
16.6. Revise up to five regulations and policies on harmful subsidies and incentives using green criteria

SECTORAL_11.text: Increase forest cover to 9% of national territory through reforestation, supporting natural forest regeneration, and strengthening forest protection measures, thereby increasing carbon dioxide sequestration.
SECTORAL_11.activities:
Conduct reforestation and afforestation programmes
Support natural forest regeneration and expansion
Strengthen forest protection against fire, illegal logging, and pest outbreaks
Establish forest agroparks to reduce direct harvesting pressure

NBSAP_13.text: By 2030, establish systems to monitor and transparently report the impacts, risks, and outcomes of business activities regarding biodiversity.
NBSAP_13.activities:
13.1. Create an incentive system to support biodiversity-friendly start-ups
13.2. Develop and introduce financial products dedicated to biodiversity conservation
13.3. Assess contributions of businesses to conservation and increase the number of enterprises eligible for tax incentives
13.4. Adopt international sustainability standards, including standards for reporting environmental impacts under international financial reporting frameworks

NBSAP_19.text: By 2030, data and information relevant to biodiversity and ecosystem services are widely accessible to decision makers, scientists and the public to guide effective and equitable governance, integrated and participatory management of biodiversity.
NBSAP_19.activities:
19.1. Conduct trainings and outreach to promote sustainable use of natural resources, associated traditional knowledge related to genetic resources, prevention of illegal wildlife and plant trade, and awareness on LMOs and alien species
19.2. Increase access to information and conduct trainings and outreach among customs, judiciary, prosecutors, environmental police and relevant public officials on prevention of illegal wildlife and plant trade and environmental crimes and offences
19.3. Promote nature-based solutions and green technologies through multi-stakeholder outreach and encourage active participation
19.4. Broadcast environmental news, information and educational programmes for at least 2 per cent of total airtime on Mongolia’s national public radio and television
19.5. Organize multi-stakeholder campaigns on environmentally friendly green technologies and encourage participation
19.6. Systematically incorporate information on the value and importance of biodiversity into editorial policies of media outlets and strengthen journalists’ capacity
19.7. Establish a master’s programme in environmental journalism and train specialized journalists

FSS_20.text: To develop domestic fertiliser production to replenish soil nutrients and increase crop quality and yield, thereby replacing imports, To develop the technical and economic feasibility of establishing nitrogen and phosphorus fertiliser plants based on mining enterprises to support exports, and to ensure their implementation.
FSS_20.activities:
To research the reserves of raw materials for nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium fertilisers based on mining deposits, and to develop the technical and economic feasibility for establishing a production plant.
Provide fertiliser on preferential terms

NRVTS_15.text: Develop legal instruments and/or establish mechanism for sustainable pastureland use.

FSS_41.text: To organise training, publicity and educational activities on the proper, appropriate and civilised consumption of food and drink.
FSS_41.activities:
Provide support for activities that promote educational and awareness-raising initiatives on the proper consumption of food and drink organised by citizens, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and institutions.
As part of its social responsibility, include the ‘Food Safety Hour’ programme in all television and radio schedules at fixed times each week, involving the public in efforts to promote proper food consumption.
Organise targeted measures to enhance public food and nutrition education.

NDC_1.text: Expand the legal protection of land by enlarging the boundaries of protected areas, designating ecological corridors, and enabling species migration and movement. This will improve the adaptive capacity and resilience of biodiversity vulnerable to climate change.

FSS_24.text: Within the framework of the policy and activities to implement the ‘Billion Trees’ national movement, establish 30 hectares of agroforestry in the provincial centre and 10 hectares in the district centre, respectively, a fruit and berry seedling propagation centre, develop nursery enterprises, and fence off agricultural fields to establish forest belts
FSS_24.sourceLabel: 3.10 Billion Trees agroforestry: 30 ha aimag, 10 ha soum
FSS_24.activities:
Establish forest belts on agricultural fields
Establish specialised fruit and berry farms, create a financing and incentive system, expand research and analysis, and develop cultivation technologies.
Establish local centres for the propagation of fruit and berry seedlings.
Establish agroforestry enterprises in provinces and municipalities to improve food security and increase exports

NBSAP_6.text: By 2030, reduce pollution from all sources to levels that are not harmful to biodiversity and ecosystem functions and human health.
NBSAP_6.activities:
6.1. Promote sound pesticide use, establish a pesticide tracking system, and introduce alternatives to chemical pesticides
6.2. Identify soil contaminated by pesticide residues and strengthen laboratory capacity to determine soil pesticide residues
6.3. Remediate soil contaminated by pesticides
6.4. Adopt international IPSM standards
6.5. Improve economic instruments for waste management and establish legal provisions based on extended producer responsibility and the polluter-pays principle
6.6. Establish temporary hazardous waste storage facilities
6.7. Translate and approve ISO standards on micro- and macroplastics in the environment
6.8. Prohibit import and use in Mongolia of chemicals newly added to Annex III of the Rotterdam Convention

NBSAP_11.text: By 2030, develop a comprehensive database for genetic resources and traditional knowledge, while strengthening legal and governance frameworks to ensure the fair and equitable sharing of benefits.
NBSAP_11.activities:
11.1. Create the legal framework for benefit-sharing from the utilization of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge
11.2. Strengthen and enrich the electronic registry on the use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge
11.3. Establish and develop a digital gene bank database, including detailed records of samples/specimens held in various collections and sequence information
11.4. Translate and approve a series of biobank standards
11.5. Establish a seed bank for wild plants
11.6. Undertake genetic evaluation of high-value livestock breeds and establish a database
11.7. Improve the legal framework governing conservation, storage, use, commercialization and benefit-sharing of food and agricultural crop genetic resources

NBSAP_17.text: Substantially and progressively increase financial resources towards biodiversity conservation from all sources, in an effective, timely, innovative and easily accessible manner.
NBSAP_17.activities:
17.1. Increase private sector financing for biodiversity within biodiversity finance systems and environmental and social responsibility frameworks
17.2. Raise public expenditure on the environment sector to internationally comparable levels as a share of GDP
17.3. Adopt the revised Law on Natural Resource Use Fees and strengthen implementation
17.4. Transition total environmental sector financing to results-based budgeting
17.5. Comprehensively upgrade the budget and expenditure database for environmental protection and restoration measures by linking it with databases and systems of other government agencies
17.6. Establish the legal basis to collect a “Nature Benefit Fee” from foreign citizens and allocate it to biodiversity conservation
17.7. Increase conservation revenues by strengthening the legal framework and implementation of biodiversity offsetting
17.8. Study and pilot biodiversity credits and other innovative mechanisms for biodiversity action
